text:
maria: heads-up: after the kernel-picker alignment change i see steady gpu memory growth on a long-running stress job. not a hard OOM yet but resident keeps climbing.

maria: changed allocator alignment to 256 -> 512 in #kernel-picker last week; suspecting staging/pinned buffer retention.

drew: can you repro locally? which job config?

maria: yes i have a minimal repro. runs a batched chat workload with our prefetcher + async uploader. instrumented with simple loop.

maria: repro command:
```bash
PYTHONPATH=. python tests/repro/pinned_staging_repro.py --iters 1000 --batch-size 16 --prefetch 2
```

maria: core of the script (very small):
```py
for i in range(iters):
    inputs = make_batch(batch_size)
    model.encode_async(inputs)  # kicks off prefetch into pinned staging buffers
    out = model.step(inputs)
    # intentionally not waiting on uploader futures in repro
```

anya: quick q — you saw the growth only with the new alignment? any diff if you revert to 256?

maria: yes revert to 256 stops the creeping after warmup. with 512 it keeps + ~30MB every 100 iters.

ben: what do nv-smi / allocator stats show?

maria: snapshot during run:
```
$ nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used --format=csv
memory.used [MiB]
24576 MiB
24608 MiB
24640 MiB
...
```

maria: allocator debug: `pinned_pool: total_reserved=25064832KB free=2048KB held=25062784KB` — held grows over time.

szymon: that sounds like pinned staging buffers are not returned to pool because of async free ordering vs kernel completion. alignment change could shift object offsets so that coalescing / free fast-path misses.

drew: put a quick instrument: log when uploader future completes and when buffer free called. any mismatch?

maria: did that. uploader completions match, but free calls are delayed and sometimes batched. here's the trace around one spike:
```
[12:02:01] uploader: enqueue pinned buf id=0x7fabc000
[12:02:01] cuda: kernel launch id=42 seq=100
[12:02:02] uploader: future done buf id=0x7fabc000
[12:02:05] allocator: free called buf id=0x7fabc000 (delayed by 3s)
```

anya: 3s delay is huge. what's blocking the free path? GC thread starved?

ben: also check async cudaFreeAsync behavior — in our runtime free may be enqueued on a stream that is not drained until later due to kernel batching heuristic. kernel-picker change touched stream affinities maybe.

maria: i instrumented stream usage: the uploader frees on stream S1, but kernel batching affined kernels to S0 and we only drain S1 on sync points which are rare in this workload. alignment change increased kernel vector size so fewer syncs -> longer hold.

szymon: aha. so not a true leak, it's delayed release because of stream / sync scheduling + pinned staging buffers require cudaFreeAsync which depends on stream draining.

drew: nice find. quick mitigation: ensure uploader frees on a stream with periodic drain or call cudaDeviceFlushCallbacks? alternatively, have allocator track outstanding refs and force release if pool exceeds threshold.

maria: i prototyped forcing timely release by moving free to a dedicated 'release' stream that we periodically synchronize every 200ms. the resident stops creeping in 1k iters test.

ben: can we make that config-driven? default behavior should avoid regressions after kernel-picker changes.

anya: also add a regression test that runs the repro for 500 iters and asserts resident delta < 100MB. quick CI job flagged on PR.

maria: opening PR with two commits: 1) use dedicated release stream for pinned frees, 2) add quick mem-reg test + comment explaining the kernel-picker interaction.

infra-bot: ci-run queued: #mem-regression-1968456789 (will run on devcluster-4).

maria: thanks all. if this looks sane i'll land later today and backport to latest stable. follow-up: we should audit other places using cudaFreeAsync and stream affinities.

ben: ping me on PR, i'll add allocator threshold fallback.

szymon: i'll add a short note to runtime docs about stream-safety and pinned buffer lifecycle.

maria: cool — will post results after CI completes. :thumbsup:
